links.function: detecting threat and separation distress the instant a trusted caregiver leaves the room
links.scene: Crimson-red subsurface pulse ignites deep inside both temporal lobes of the contained living 3D brain the moment the clinic door clicks shut
links.narration_bridge: Deep inside each side of the brain, the amygdala, the emotional alarm, fires the second the door clicks shut.

links.function: sending calming top-down safety signals to quiet the amygdala during caregiver reunion
links.scene: Electric cyan-blue pathways shine just above the eye sockets and travel backward to dim the crimson-red amygdala during a warm caregiver embrace
links.narration_bridge: Just behind the eyes, the ventromedial prefrontal cortex, the social brake, borrows the parent's calm to switch that alarm off.

links.function: triggering stress hormone cascades that keep heart rate and cortisol elevated in avoidant infants
links.scene: Warm amber-gold and crimson-red glow persists in the deep central hypothalamus below the thalamus while outward cortical motor strips clamp still
links.narration_bridge: Below the relay hub, the hypothalamus, the hormone control center, keeps pumping stress signals for thirty minutes.

links.function: registering social separation distress and effortful suppression of crying
links.scene: Contained amber-gold signal tension courses along the inner medial wall above the corpus callosum as the toddler turns away from the doorway
links.narration_bridge: Along the inner wall, the anterior cingulate cortex, the conflict detector, strains to hold every tear inside.
